description: Ratchet algorithm registry. Every entry is a claim about cryptography; see CONTRIBUTING.md before changing one.

quantum.broken: Shor's algorithm breaks it outright. Must migrate.
quantum.reduced: Grover halves the effective security. Usually fine at higher parameter sizes, but worth recording.

classical.broken: Already broken today, independent of quantum.

field_notes.nist_quantum_security_level: NIST PQC security category written to CycloneDX nistQuantumSecurityLevel: 0 meets no category, 1 to 5 as defined by NIST's PQC evaluation criteria. The entry's value applies when the parameter set is unknown and is the lowest category any common parameter set reaches; parameter_sets overrides it when the parameter set is known.
field_notes.oid: OID of the algorithm. null when no single OID identifies it without information Ratchet does not detect; oid_note says why.
field_notes.parameter_sets: Optional. Keyed by the parameterSetIdentifier Ratchet records; each may set its own oid and nist_quantum_security_level.

RSA.replacement: ML-KEM-768 for key establishment, ML-DSA-65 for signatures
RSA.why: Shor's algorithm factors the modulus in polynomial time.

ECDSA.oid_note: An ECDSA signature OID names the hash as well as the algorithm (for example ecdsa-with-SHA256, 1.2.840.10045.4.3.2, RFC 5758). The hash is not detected, so no OID is claimed. 1.2.840.10045.4 is the parent arc, not an algorithm.
ECDSA.replacement: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), or SLH-DSA if you need hash-based
ECDSA.why: Shor's algorithm solves the discrete log on the curve.

ECDH.replacement: ML-KEM-768, ideally hybrid X25519+ML-KEM during transition
ECDH.why: Shor's algorithm solves the discrete log on the curve.

EC.replacement: determine usage before migrating, ML-DSA-65 if signing, ML-KEM-768 if key agreement
EC.why: Shor's algorithm solves the discrete log on the curve. Whether this key signs or agrees keys was not visible to the scanner, and the migration target depends on which.

Ed25519.why: Edwards-curve discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm.

X25519.why: Curve25519 discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm.

Ed448.why: Edwards448 discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm.

X448.why: Curve448 discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm.

EdDSA.oid_note: Ed25519 is 1.3.101.112 and Ed448 is 1.3.101.113 (RFC 8410); the curve was not visible to the scanner.
EdDSA.replacement: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204), or ML-DSA-87 if the curve is Ed448
EdDSA.why: Edwards-curve discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm. The curve, Ed25519 or Ed448, was not visible to the scanner.

XDH.oid_note: X25519 is 1.3.101.110 and X448 is 1.3.101.111 (RFC 8410); the curve was not visible to the scanner.
XDH.replacement: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203), or ML-KEM-1024 if the curve is X448
XDH.why: Montgomery-curve discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm. The curve, X25519 or X448, was not visible to the scanner.

DH.why: Shor's algorithm solves the finite-field discrete log.

DSA.why: Shor's algorithm solves the finite-field discrete log.

MD5.replacement: SHA-256 or SHA-3, or BLAKE2 for non-compliance use
MD5.why: Collisions are practical today. Quantum is not the problem here.

SHA-1.why: Chosen-prefix collisions demonstrated in 2020. Retire it.

3DES.why: Sweet32 birthday attacks. Disallowed by NIST for encryption after 2023.

RC4.why: Biased keystream. Prohibited in TLS since RFC 7465.

AES.oid_note: An AES OID names key size and mode together (for example aes128-GCM, 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1.6). Mode is not detected, so no OID is claimed. 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.1 is the parent arc.
AES.why: Grover halves effective key length. AES-256 stays at 128-bit margin.

SHA-256.why: Grover gives a quadratic speedup only. Still acceptable.

ML-KEM.oid_note: Each ML-KEM parameter set has its own OID, listed under parameter_sets. 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.4 is the parent arc.

ML-DSA.oid_note: Each ML-DSA parameter set has its own OID, listed under parameter_sets. 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3 is NIST's signature-algorithms arc, shared with DSA, ECDSA and RSA variants and with SLH-DSA.
